headline: New Urine Test Spots Bladder Cancer with 92% Accuracy
meta_description: A UK trial shows the Galeas urine test correctly identifies over 92% of bladder cancer cases, potentially sparing patients from invasive procedures.
summary_short: A new at-home urine test has proven 92.2% accurate at detecting bladder cancer in a UK trial, offering hope for faster, less invasive diagnoses.
body:
A new urine test has proven highly effective at detecting bladder cancer, with trials showing it correctly identified 92.2% of cancer cases. The Galeas urine test was trialled on 964 patients across seven urology departments in England and Scotland in a study led by the University of Birmingham.

The breakthrough centres on simplicity: an at-home test that could spare patients from undergoing invasive diagnostic procedures. Experts have welcomed the results as a step toward speedier diagnoses, addressing a key challenge in early cancer detection where delays can significantly impact treatment outcomes.

While the snippet ends mid-sentence, the core finding is striking—a non-invasive screening method with accuracy above 92% could reshape how bladder cancer is initially identified, potentially moving diagnosis from hospital procedures to patients' homes.

Trial included 964 patients across England and Scotland
Study led by University of Birmingham
At-home test could replace invasive procedures
